market_holds: Spot $1.21 (sealed baseline as of 2026-11-13 18:14 UTC; intraday, not the close). That is 89% below the 52-week high, -6.9% over 5 days and +4.3% over 20 days, with 20-day realised vol at 96% annualised (about 6% a day). There is no usable option chain: 16 contracts of open interest and no two-sided ATM quote, so the market has priced no implied move. Over 8 prints the median reaction is 3.85%. The two most recent were small: Q2 bmo +4.6% and Q1 bmo -3.1%. The same quarter a year ago (Q3 2025) fell 21.45% on a revenue miss of about 42% against a stale consensus, and January 2026 fell 40% on a $75m equity offering announced with preliminary Q4 results. Consensus comes from one or two analysts: Q3 EPS about -$0.29 to -$0.30 and revenue $5.5m to $6.0m (Benzinga, Chartmill, Stockalarm snippets; revision dates not visible). Q3 2025 revenue was $5.38m. There is no numeric guide. The stock trades on financing and liquidity, not on EPS. It has fallen from about $2.0 at the Q2 print to $1.13 on 2026-10-19, jumped 15% on the $60m McKinney sale-leaseback (2026-10-21) and given it back. Short interest has risen from 3.67m (2026-07-15) to 4.82m (2026-10-30), about 8.6% of shares and 12.2 days to cover (FINRA via equibles). A $25m ATM with ThinkEquity has been live since 2026-06-12.
view: The print itself (revenue of about $5-6.5m) is too small to matter. On my own arithmetic, revenue should land near the lowered consensus. Restaurant revenue was up 25% year on year in Q2, helped by Roth's Sea & Steak, which opened in November 2025. Event ticket revenue fell 27% in Q2, and Q3 2025's event line ($2.76m) is the comparison it has to beat. So revenue gives little signal either way. What the stock trades on is the funding story, and that story slipped against its own August promises. In the Q2 release (2026-08-13) management said it would 'move away from sale-leaseback to C-PACE financing'. It said more than $150m of CBRE-arranged C-PACE would close in Q3, retiring the Ryan bridge loan and the debenture, and that Regent Bank Amphitheater would open in Fall 2026. Since then: the opening slipped to 4-5 December. No C-PACE closing appears in any 8-K, and the STORE ground lease signed 2026-10-19 gives VENU a purchase option that is triggered only once it obtains a C-PACE commitment, which implies none had closed. The bridge was paid off from a $60m sale-leaseback of the McKinney land instead, plus a $7.5m Centennial sale-leaseback. The company handed back the $12.5m debenture holdback and is paying the remaining $12.5m in cash at about $2.875m a month. The President left on 2026-10-13. McKinney's opening is pushed into 2027. Cash at June 30 was $16.3m after $133m of six-month capex. The 10-Q will show Sep 30 cash before the October transactions, any ATM use, and the going-concern paragraph, which management called 'alleviated' in Q2 on the strength of C-PACE and the Fall opening. Against that, every one of these facts has been public for weeks. The stock has already lost about 40% since August and sits at a deep discount to reported assets. The release will lead with the October financings and the Broken Arrow opening, and a short of 12 days to cover can squeeze a thin stock on an upbeat call (11:00 ET, inside the window). I lean slightly down, on the chance that the 10-Q's liquidity and going-concern language, or a new raise, gets re-read on Monday morning. I cannot show that the market has missed it, so there is no recommendation.

recommendation.reason: The negative drivers (C-PACE not closed, Broken Arrow slipped to December, a pivot back to sale-leasebacks, ATM overhang, cash burn) are dated and real, but they were all public in 8-Ks and press releases weeks ago, and the stock has fallen about 40% since August. I cannot show they are unpriced. Revenue against a single-analyst consensus that was already cut looks roughly in line, and a crowded short raises the chance of an up move on an upbeat call. The direction probability is well short of 65.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: Upside: the release or 10-Q announces a closed or committed C-PACE facility, or a clean liquidity statement covering the McKinney build. Downside: the 10-Q restores 'substantial doubt' about going concern, or the release comes with an equity raise.

self_critique: The strongest case against a lean-down view: the October financings ($60m McKinney, $7.5m Centennial, $5m Aramark, the debenture halved) materially de-risk the 12-month liquidity picture. Management will lead the call with the Broken Arrow opening three weeks out and FireSuite sales. A short base of 12 days to cover on a $70m company can produce a sharp up move on any reassuring liquidity sentence. And the stock already trades as if it were distressed. The case for a stronger down call is the 10-Q's liquidity note and a possible restoration of going-concern doubt, which this company's history (January) shows can move the stock by tens of percent. Both are plausible, so I stay near 50.
